claim: Skype for Windows 4.0 launched February 3, 2009
Skype 4.0 introduced a new bandwidth manager for quality video calling on low bandwidth
Skype 4.0 added a guided setup flow for new users (download, mic/webcam/headset/audio test)
Skype 4.0 included Smart Help feature flagging sound problems during calls
Skype 4.0 introduced a Conversations tab
Skype 4.2.0.158 for Windows released April 8, 2010
Skype 4.2 fixed spurious old authorization request notifications after upgrading from 4.1
Skype 4.2 known issue running Cyberlink YouCam video decoration software
Skype 4.2 known issue: screen sharing to 4.0 or lower fails to show video on Pentium 4/3 receivers
Wikipedia dates a Skype 4.0 screenshot caption to 2009
Skype Chat Support was a premium feature for Skype Premium and some other paid users
Skype 4.2.0.158 known issues also included LifeCam VX-3000 freeze and Asus Videophone call issues
Skype 4.0 replaced columnar layout with dual-pane window (contact list left, detail/history right)
Skype 4.0 introduced 'conversation' concept with adjacent tab showing recent conversations
Skype 4.0 added button to detach Conversations window into separate windows
Skype 4.0 tray icon shows missed event count with stacked popup list
Skype 4.0 added Video Call button alongside Call button per contact
Skype 4.0 allows accessing audio settings from Call menu anytime, not just during calls
Skype 4.0 overhauled interface from 3.8, supported Windows 2000/2003/XP/Vista and unofficially Windows 7
Notifications category in Skype Options interface could disable unwanted in-app notifications
Skype 4.1 (2009) introduced screen sharing
Skype 4.2 (2010) supported HD video calls and added call transfer; last of 4.x series before 5.0
'Not Available' status supported since Skype 4, removed in Skype 5
'SkypeMe!' status hidden from selection starting Skype 4, removed completely in Skype 5
Skype supports ~254 static/animated emoticons
'Online' status set automatically by default, allows contact any way
'Offline' shown when Skype closed or chosen manually; cannot receive calls/IMs
'Away' indicates user stepped away, may still receive calls/messages with sound notification
'Do Not Disturb' online but notifications arrive without sound
'Invisible' uses same icon as Offline; still receives notifications
'Blocked' status shown to blocklisted users who see blocker as Offline
'Unauthorized' applies to users not on contact list; messages/calls received only if security settings allow
'Forwarding' status: Offline but call forwarding set up so calls still reach user
'Connecting' is the only animated status icon, shown when Skype can't connect to internet
Away auto-activates via configurable idle timer at Tools > Settings > General
/add username(s) chat command adds users to chat, multiple separated by spaces
/kick and /kickban chat commands remove a user from group chat
/get role displays current user's role, set via /setrole
/history loads entire correspondence history in active chat window
/get masters, /get helpers, /get listeners display lists of users with those chat roles
/set allowlist and /set banlist manage who may join or is barred from a chat
Not all listed chat commands are supported in all Skype versions
Skype 4.0 added a big green Video Call button putting video calling front and center
Skype 4.0 offered picture-in-picture video, movable self-view thumbnail
Skype 4.0 beta supported up to 25 participants in voice-only group call; video remained one-to-one
Skype president said prior UI was purpose-built for voice, explaining 4.0 redesign toward video
Video Call button appeared alongside Call button for each contact in Skype 4.0
Skype 4.0 let users place SkypeOut calls/texts or buy SkypeIn number for calls/voicemail
Skype 4.0 tray icon shows missed event count (call, voicemail, IM) with stacked popup
Skype 4.0 used adaptive bandwidth manager to preserve audio/video quality under limited bandwidth
Skype 4.2 supported HD (720p) video calling at up to 22fps with certified webcams with H.264 processor
Skype 4.2 HD video used H.264 with legacy VP7 (CPU) or VP8 as alternatives
SkypeOut allowed calling landline/mobile phones including international at discounted rates via Skype Credit or subscription
SkypeIn (renamed Online Number, later Skype Number) let users receive calls to a Skype-provided number; called SkypeIn until 2010
Skype 2.0+ supported Skype-to-Skype video calling between two parties on Windows/Mac/Linux
Group video calling not introduced until Skype 5, implying 4.x group calls stayed voice-only
Screen sharing was originally a premium feature (up to 10 people), made free with group video in summer 2014
H1 2010 Skype had 124M monthly connected users and 8.1M paying users, up from 91M/6.6M in H2 2009
